headline: OVMS continuous-batching serving of Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B int4 at GPU OFFLOAD_RATIO=30 measured 1.71 tok/s median against a 38.58 tok/s same-server same-model baseline — a ~21x regression — with no system-memory saving. Rolled back the same night.

contrast_with_prior_in_house_result.harness: openvino_genai LLMPipeline directly, Python 3.14.3, fresh venv, OpenVINO 2026.3.1
contrast_with_prior_in_house_result.note: That campaign measured int4@30 as FASTER than fully resident (+14%). This run contradicts it by ~17x on the same feature, same ratio, same model family, same box — the salient difference being the serving stack (OVMS continuous batching + prefix caching + u8 KV cache) versus a single-stream LLMPipeline.

leading_hypothesis_UNTESTED: OVMS continuous batching may defeat the offload LRU expert cache: concurrent/streamed requests touching different experts would thrash a cache sized for one stream. Plausible, consistent with both datasets, and NOT measured here.
not_measured: A clean-box run. The measured box had 0.64 GiB free and 30.68 GiB in use; the 38.58 baseline's box state is not recorded in its JSON.
An OVMS 2026.3 run at OFFLOAD_RATIO=0, which is the control that would separate the version change from the offload change. This is the single most important missing arm.
int8 (excluded deliberately: the prior campaign's Finding 1 documents an int8 second-generate hang that breaks multi-generate agentic use).
Concurrency sweep - the batching hypothesis above is untested.
Prefill/TTFT with a controlled prompt set; the TTFT figures here are incidental.
Disk contention state on the NVMe the experts stream from.
honest_limits: N=3 with small completion counts (35-81 tokens), one warmup, no cooldown discipline, and a dirty box. This is strong enough to justify an immediate rollback and NOT strong enough to publish as a characterisation of the feature. The 2026.3-at-ratio-0 control must run before any claim is made about whether the regression is caused by offload or by the version change.
